bank.q: Consider the following statements about the 42nd Amendment's legacy:
s: Article 31C's extension to all Directive Principles survives.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Minerva Mills struck down the extension of Article 31C, leaving only the pre-42nd position covering Articles 39(b) and (c).

bank.q: Match List I (concept or body) with List II (origin):
pairs: 2. George Grote, writing on Athenian democracy
bank.e: Grote's phrase, South Africa's doctrine, the Soviet model for duties, and Article 148 for the CAG.

bank.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The CAG's recommendations carry no binding enforcement power
Naz Foundation was reversed by Koushal and then restored by Navtej
The 42nd Amendment moved education to the Concurrent List
Constitutional morality is expressly defined in the Constitution
bank.e: It appears nowhere in the text — the source of both its flexibility and the criticism of judicial subjectivity.

bank.as: Both transformative constitutionalism and constitutional morality place the Constitution above prevailing social consensus.
bank.rs: Each was invoked in Navtej Singh Johar and Sabarimala to override popular morality in favour of dignity and equality.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the two doctrines operate as complementary parts of the same interpretive project.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about accountability institutions:
s: The CAG's salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
CAG reports on State accounts are laid before the State Legislature.
The CAG may compel departments to act on its findings.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. There is no binding power — enforcement depends entirely on the Public Accounts Committee and executive responsiveness.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) → Minerva Mills (1980) → Naz Foundation (2009) → Puttaswamy (2017).

bank.q: Which of the following pairs correctly links an audit to its consequence?
o: 2G Spectrum — cancellation of 214 coal block allocations
Coalgate — cancellation of over 200 coal block allocations
Commonwealth Games — cancellation of spectrum auctions
bank.e: The 2G report led to 122 telecom licences being cancelled; the Coalgate report to 214 coal block allocations being declared illegal.

bank.q: All of the following were reversed after 1976 EXCEPT:
o: Article 257A on central forces without state consent
Article 368(4) barring judicial review of amendments
bank.e: Part IV-A survives, as do Articles 39A, 43A and the tribunals provisions.

bank.as: Judicial recognition of a right does not guarantee its realisation.
bank.rs: Manual scavenging persists despite Article 17 and repeated court orders.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the recurring gap between constitutional pronouncement and executive enforcement.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the interpretive evolution of the Constitution:
s: A. K. Gopalan represents the literal phase of interpretation.
Kesavananda introduced structural and purposive interpretation.
Puttaswamy overruled Gopalan's approach to personal liberty.
bank.e: All three are correct — Maneka Gandhi had already displaced Gopalan's compartmentalised reading, and Puttaswamy completed the shift on privacy.
